title: Asita's tears, in verse
hook: the sage weeps that he will not hear the child teach (Buddhacarita 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the birth, in verse, a newborn who stands and walks. Your line: seven steps.

A palace celebrating a new baby, and a guest nobody sent for: an old holy man, Asita, who has seen signs and come on his own. The king receives him with honor and brings out the child. Asita looks for a long time. And his eyes fill, and the tears run down. In a room like that, a holy man weeping over a newborn seems to mean only one thing. Year one met Asita in a few lines. The poem gives the scene room, and lets both men speak: a frightened father, and an old man who has to explain his tears.
screen: `A HOLY MAN NOBODY SENT FOR.` → `HE LOOKS, AND WEEPS.` → `A FATHER AFRAID.`

segments.voice: First, the king's fear. King Shuddhodana sees the tears and trembles. Is my son's life short, he asks; is some harm coming to him? It is the question a parent asks. Second, Asita's answer. Not for the child, he says. The child is well, and more than well. He will leave the kingdom behind, wake up, and teach a way out of suffering for the world. In the poem's image, paraphrased here, the teaching will be like a boat that carries people across a great flood. Third, the turn. Then why weep? Because I am old, Asita says. My time is nearly over. This child will teach, and I won't be alive to hear it. The tears are for himself. He arrived at the right house, too early in the story. He doesn't resent the child or pretend not to care. He weeps honestly, and he blesses what he won't share. And fourth, the shadow. In front of the king, Asita has said the boy will leave the kingdom. A father who wanted an heir has just heard he may be raising a wanderer, and that sentence will sit in the palace for years. Some people know a version of Asita's grief: a grandparent who won't see the wedding, a founder who won't see the school finished. His answer is to love it anyway, from where he stands.
screen: `IS MY SON IN DANGER?` · `NOT FOR THE CHILD.` · `I WON'T LIVE TO HEAR HIM.` · `THE BOY WILL LEAVE THE KINGDOM.` · then, large: `BORN TOO EARLY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a teacher you'll never meet: a writer long gone, a grandparent's grandparent whose sayings got passed down, or someone not yet born who will teach what you can't. Let that person sit in the room with you; you don't have to say anything. Just let there be gratitude, and a little of Asita's ache, side by side.
Asita's tears. An old sage weeps over the newborn, not from fear for the child, but because he won't live to hear him teach. Today's word.
Your line: born too early. An old man's tears, and a blessing. Day six hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Asita's visit is told in other Buddhist texts besides this poem, and it appears in paintings and carvings of the Buddha's early life.

chat.says: Why did the old sage cry when he saw the baby Buddha?
options: He was old, and wouldn't live to hear the child teach.
He saw the child would die young, and feared for him.
He wept for the king, who would lose his only heir.
chat.meaning: Asita tells the frightened king the child is well. He weeps for himself, too old to hear the boy teach.
